source_text: Hic autem breviter admonuerim, quoniam suffragari tibi non potest ad eius sententiae confirmationem, quam omnis eruditio, omnis ratio, et lex Dei convincit iniquissimam. Diligens ergo lector intendat quod pronuntiasti, Deum esse factorem malorum; et tales eum condere, qui sine aliquo propriae merito voluntatis eant in condemnationem prorsus omnes.
pass_a_gloss: Here however I would briefly have warned, that it cannot vote for you toward the confirmation of that sentence, which all learning, all reason, and the law of God convicts most unjust. Let therefore a diligent reader intend what you pronounced, that God is the maker of evils; and that he founds such, who without some desert of their own will go into condemnation outright all.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS meritum=desert; Blaise without later merit-system

pass_b_english: Here I would briefly warn that it cannot support you in establishing an opinion which all learning, all reason, and God's Law convict of being utterly unjust. Let the attentive reader therefore notice your declaration that God is the maker of evil people, and creates people of such a kind that, without anything deserved by a will of their own, absolutely all of them go into condemnation.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Glossary: avoid modern merit-theology; Julian means deserved outcome.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
